narrative.overview: The site reads like the sports section of a newspaper about one player: you. Headlines are set big and condensed, numbers are the stars, and every panel sits under a thick black rule. The mood is cocky but clear: poster type and big numbers give it swagger, while body text, labels and tables stay calm and plain. There is a light edition on warm newsprint and a dark edition on near-black paper; the same paper with ink and stock swapped.
keyCharacteristics: Anton poster type for headlines, player types and every big number; Geist for everything you read.
Warm newsprint (or night paper), ink, and one signal orange.
A heavy rule across the top of each panel instead of boxes and shadows.
Stats with labels: small uppercase tracked labels over large condensed numbers.
Green and red only ever mean won/right and lost/wrong.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange is the only accent. Anything orange is either what you are working on or a link; nothing is orange for decoration.

rules.name: The Results Only Rule
rules.body: Green and red are reserved for won/lost and right/wrong, always with a label, number or letter beside them.

rules.name: The No White Rule
rules.body: Paper is never pure white and night paper is never pure black; the warmth is the newsprint.

rules.name: The Number Leads Rule
rules.body: A stat is a large Anton number with a small uppercase label; never a number without its label.

rules.name: The Shout Once Rule
rules.body: One display line per view; everything under it is body or label.

rules.name: The Even Grid Rule
rules.body: Repeated items are equal tiles in a grid; explanations open from one button rather than making tiles uneven.

rules.name: The Rule Not Box Rule
rules.body: A panel is defined by its 3px ink rule on top and its paper tone; no outlines or shadows on panels.

dos: Do set every headline, player type and big number in Anton, uppercase, and everything else in Geist.
Do put a 3px ink rule across the top of every panel and keep panels flat.
Do keep orange for what the player is working on and for links, and darken it to Readable Orange when it is text.
Do give every number a label and every colour a word or letter beside it.
Do keep the dark edition as the same paper with ink and stock swapped.
Do keep the board Lichess's brown board with cburnett pieces.
donts: Don't use pure white or pure black backgrounds.
Don't add a second accent colour or use green and red for anything but results.
Don't put shadows or outlines around panels; only the player card and floating menus lift off the page.
Don't go "gamer": no neon, glows, pixel fonts or holographic effects (tried and rejected).
Don't let a long explanation make tiles uneven; hide it behind one button instead.
